title: Bridge from Corpus Pane knowledge to the eventual 2D poser
plainLanguage: The Corpus Pane’s long-term payoff is a poser where a torso, arm, leg, head, and face can be chosen from compatible view families, attached to the same skeleton, and given small tested adjustments.
purpose: Define the path from evidence collection to reusable character construction.

rules.statement: Do not turn every reviewed configuration into artwork automatically. A reviewed skeletal configuration and a reusable painted part are different deliverables.
For each high-value configuration, identify whether existing doll artwork can represent it, can represent it with bounded articulation, or requires a new part variant.
A poser part must pass compatibility tests against its host body/view before entering the approved mix-and-match pool.
Use semantic sockets to keep anatomy stable while swapping view-specific artwork.
Keep pose, artwork, attachment, layer order, and articulation records linked but independently reviewable.

implementation.currentSupport: The still mannequin rig already has modular layers, anchors and pivots; Corpus Pane already has reviewed regional configurations.
implementation.futureWork: Create a bounded arm–torso pilot before broad part harvesting.
